title: Missing legacy records left the sources of a $2 million street-tree balance uncertain

beats.text: One San Francisco report closed its street tree fee account at $79,273.

visual.sub: The earlier edition closed the street-tree account at $79,273

beats.text: The next report opened the following year at just over two million dollars.
The Controller said some old accounting records were unavailable after a system change.

visual.kicker: The next opening balance could include penalties as well as fees

beats.text: The starting amount likely included other revenue, such as penalties for removed trees.

visual.kicker: The next opening balance could include penalties as well as fees

beats.text: For five fiscal years, published fee receipts match the City revenue register.

visual.kicker: Five years of fee receipts agree with the register; the sixth differs

beats.text: In fiscal 2025, they differ by about $25,000.
That difference calls for the individual entries behind the two figures.

visual.kicker: Five years of fee receipts agree with the register; the sixth differs

beats.text: In 2026 the City established a separate account for qualifying new fees.
The ordinance restricts that money to planting and watering trees for three years.

visual.kicker: A later ordinance created a separate account for qualifying new fees

beats.text: The new account does not explain what was in the old one.

visual.kicker: A later ordinance created a separate account for qualifying new fees
